ops.title: Incident 2026-07-03: NFS cutover CPU spike + holder saturation
ops.body:
All 10 pool accounts re-fused onto fuse-t/go-nfsv4 mirrors ~02:44; by 03:30 active claude
sessions burned ~440% CPU, load hit 25, acct-08 mirror wedged (metadata OK, reads hung) under
5 live sessions, acct-01 dead under 3, recurring "holder may be saturated" liveness failures.

Measured: open+close through a mount 1.4-3.4ms vs 7µs local; negative lookup 320-570µs
(nonegnamecache, never cached); repeated stat 2µs (client attr cache fine); merged .claude.json
375KB @ 1.3ms/read; ~300 GETATTR/s fleet-sustained. claude (Bun) fans fs syscalls across 18+
pool threads; the syscall system time is the visible CPU.

Root causes (both fixed in fusekit v0.27.0/v0.28.0; full mechanism notes in the FUSEKIT repo's
cc-notes doc 130274e):
1. Holder self-demoted to the Darwin background band (fusekit v0.23.0), inherited by all
   go-nfsv4 servers — the data plane throttled below the sessions it served; starved under
   load; band externally unclearable (restart-only). Fixed: proc.Nice(5) in fusekit v0.27.0.
2. fuse-t silly-rename of open synth files moved the ACCOUNT-PRIVATE merged .claude.json into
   shared ~/.claude as .fuse_hidden* (privacy leak, readable via every account's mount; 4 ×
   ~489KB in 13 min). Fixed: holderfs diverts the silly-rename class to privateRoot
   (fusekit v0.28.0, VM-gated).

Ruled out: go-nfsv4 attrcache (VM-proven torn reads for synth-document mounts at any TTL —
cc-pool never opts in; pinned by TestOverlaySpecNeverOptsIntoAttrCache).

Deploy: requires a zero-live-session window (holder replace tears down/remounts all mounts);
backlog task ff181f3. Residual by design: ~200µs/op transport floor at normal priority; next
lever if needed is negative-lookup caching (no fuse-t knob today — upstream ask).
